content:
gina: Heads up — customer onlineshop-prod reporting inconsistent embedding shapes between Hosted and Dedicated when calling /v1/embeddings. Hosted returns 768, Dedicated returns 512 for same payload. Also seeing a bunch of 502/504 timeouts from Dedicated in the last hour.
JordanM: Ugh. Do we know the model name/variant they're hitting?
gina: They say model=redwood-open-embed, no explicit quant flag. Sample payload attached (inline): `[{\"input\":\"redwood rocks\"}]`.
SamSRE: Any request headers they set? routing tag, tenant, or content-type oddities?
gina: They use API key for a customer account that has both Hosted and Dedicated enabled. No custom headers other than Authorization and Content-Type: application/json.
JordanM: Likely routing mismatch to different model variants (512 vs 768 dims). Could be that Hosted is on "open-embed-768" and Dedicated got pinned to an older 512 variant. Also the timeouts hint at incorrect autoscale / cold-starts on Dedicated.
AlanBilling: Billing spike noticed for that org around the same time — lots of retries/resends. We need to capture request_ids to reconcile.
gina: Customer provided one request_id: req_20240614_aa742. It maps to a 200 with 768 vectors on Hosted and a 200 with 512 on Dedicated.
SamSRE: Can we repro locally with their API key? If not, ask them for a small repro snippet and exact timestamps. Also check routing logs: `kubectl logs -lapp=routing -n prod --since=2h | grep req_20240614_aa742`
JordanM: Also check model catalog mapping service: `GET /internal/catalog/models/redwood-open-embed` — verify alias -> artifact mapping. If Dedicated host is pinned to an artifact with a different architecture, dims will differ.
gina: Running their minimal curl now: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-open-embed","input":"test embedding"}'```
deploybot: deploy event: dedicated-pool-3 autoscaler scaled from 2 -> 6 at 2024-06-14T15:12:04Z :rocket:
SamSRE: Re: timeouts — check the Dedicated ingress / envoy logs for 502 root cause. Could be backend returning 504 due to KV cache miss combined with long quantized init.
JordanM: One quick debug: ask customer to include header `X-Model-Variant: stable` to force aliasing, or `X-Routing-Force: hosted` to confirm parity. If dims match when forcing, this is a routing artifact.
gina: Customer tried `X-Routing-Force: dedicated` and got 512 dims. `X-Routing-Force: hosted` returns 768 dims.
AlanBilling: I'll flag the invoice anomaly but hold charges until we confirm it's a retry storm. Please add the charge_handoff tag to the ticket.
SamSRE: Can engineering run a consistency check across environments: sample 100 inputs, call the same model alias against hosted/dedicated/private and compare lengths + cosine drift. I can schedule a job.
JordanM: Also look for quantization/compile-time differences. The Dedicated artifact might be a quantized 8-bit variant (hence 512 output) — check the model build metadata: `artifact_metadata.sha` and `quantization` flag.
gina: I pulled the artifact metadata for the Dedicated host: shows `artifact:v1.3-quant8` whereas Hosted points at `artifact:v1.3-fp16`. That explains values but not dims — unless the quant build used a truncated head.
SamSRE: Good find. If the artifact actually changes architecture (head dims), that's a model onboarding bug — catalog allowed a variant with different output shape under same alias. Need immediate rollback to `artifact:v1.3-fp16` for Dedicated.
JordanM: Next steps: 1) Roll back Dedicated alias to `v1.3-fp16` (canary 10%), 2) Run parity job comparing top-5 nearest neighbor similarity for 1000 sample queries, 3) Add validation in catalog to reject artifacts with mismatched output dims for same alias.
gina: I've filed a support ticket #SUP-87321 and put customer on hold for a maintenance window. I attached sample payloads and their request_ids.
AlanBilling: Noted. I'll pause billing for the retry window and mark it investigation.pending.
SamSRE: For the timeout/errors — after rollback, monitor dedicated ingress latencies: `sum(rate(envoy_response_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)` and alert if p95 > 500ms.
JordanM: Also add a quick unit check in model onboarding that runs a small embed call against a golden input and assert dims == alias.expected_dim. If mismatch, block rollout.
gina: Customer ok with canary rollback. I'll coordinate the window. Thanks all. :pray:
eva_prod_monitor: Alert summary — Dedicated pool: increased 502s from 0.1% -> 3.4% between 15:05-15:25 UTC, matching the timeframe above.
SamSRE: I'll own postmortem and link logs + rollout timeline. Jordan, can you own the catalog fix?
JordanM: Yep taking catalog fix, will PR validation and a migration script to reconcile aliases.
gina: Closing loop with customer: will update in 30m after canary rollback. Will paste final notes here. :white_check_mark:
